transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. I'm mostly here because my sleep has gotten really unreliable lately. Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there replaying sales forecasts and issues with my team. And then I usually end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again after that.
Besides work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other areas of your life?

Yeah, it definitely jumps around. Most days, my mind will go from whether we'll hit our launch numbers to worrying if someone on my team is about to quit. And then it shifts to things like the mortgage, or a client renewal. It just feels like... like every small delay could turn into something major, no matter what part of my life it is.
How long have you been experiencing this excessive, hard-to-control worry?

It's been building for a while now. I'd say... well, it really started right around the time we had a reorganization in the sales division. That was about thirteen months ago, and it's just been pretty constant since then.
Do you often feel physically tense, keyed up, or unable to relax?

Yeah, pretty much all the time. I just feel... wound up. It's like I'm sitting in a high-pressure pipeline review, even when I'm just at home trying to eat dinner. And my shoulders are always tight. I can't seem to get them to relax, no matter what I do.
Do you continue to feel this level of worry even during periods when the reorganization or other work problems are not actively occurring?

Yeah, it doesn't really stop, even when things are quiet at work. I can tell myself, "Brenda, you've done the plan, let it go," but... it doesn't work. Five minutes later, I'm right back in another loop. It's like I check one concern off my list, only to have three more pop up to take its place. I just can't seem to control it.
Which came first: the persistent worrying or the sleep problems?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. It all kind of... blends together at this point. I know the worrying really kicked off around that reorganization, but I couldn't tell you exactly when the sleep issues started compared to that. It feels like they've both just been happening for a long time.
Is the sales-division reorganization still ongoing?

Um, I'm not actually sure. I mean, the big announcements happened a while ago, but... they haven't officially said it's completely finished. So, honestly, I don't really know where it stands right now.
If the reorganization were definitively over, do you think your excessive worry would continue at about the same level?

I'm really not sure. Um... I'd like to think it would go away, or at least calm down a lot. But since I already worry even when things are quiet at work, I honestly don't know if my brain would just find something else to focus on. It's hard to say without it actually being over.
Before the sales-division reorganization, did you already have a pattern of excessive worry that was difficult to control?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, I've always been someone who stresses a little bit about work and life, but... I don't know if it was ever this difficult to control before the reorganization. It definitely wasn't taking up this much of my energy back then. So I can't really say for sure if there was a specific pattern of it beforehand.
Is the sales-division reorganization still actively affecting your work right now?

Well, I'm not really sure. My day-to-day tasks are mostly the same as they've been lately, so... I don't know if the reorganization itself is still directly changing my actual workload right now. It's kind of hard to separate what's just normal sales pressure and what's fallout from the restructuring at this point. So I can't really say for certain.
When you are not thinking about work or the reorganization, do you still find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life?

Yes, I do. Even if I'm not actively thinking about the reorganization, my mind just... jumps around. Like, I'll be worrying about whether we'll hit our launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm stressing about whether someone on my team is going to quit. And if it's not work, it's the mortgage, or a client renewal. It just feels like every little delay or issue could turn into some massive problem, no matter what part of my life it's in.
Has there been a continuous period of at least six months when you worried excessively about several areas of your life even though no specific stressful event was occurring?

Well, I guess... yes. It's been going on for a while now. This whole feeling, the constant worrying about everything, it's really been building up since they reorganized the sales division. That was about thirteen months ago, and it just hasn't stopped since then.
Do you find that your worrying makes it difficult to concentrate on tasks?

I don't think so, no. I mean, the worry is definitely always there in the background, but... it doesn't really stop me from focusing on what I need to do. I can still sit down and get my work done just fine, so I wouldn't say it messes with my concentration.
When work is relatively stable and no major work problems are happening, how intense is your worry compared with when the reorganization was actively occurring?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed a difference. Even when things are pretty stable and there aren't any major crises happening at work, the worry is still just... there. I wouldn't say it feels any less intense now than it did when the reorganization was actually happening.
Since the worry began, have you often felt unusually restless or unable to sit still?

Yeah, definitely. I just feel... wound up almost all the time. It's honestly like I'm sitting in a stressful pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And my shoulders just stay tight, no matter how much I try to relax or settle down.
Has the sales-division reorganization definitively ended?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um... they haven't exactly given us a clear answer on whether it's officially finished. So I don't really know if it's definitively ended or not.
During the past six months, was there a continuous period when the reorganization was no longer affecting you at all but you still worried excessively about several areas of your life?

I don't think there's been a time like that, no. Like I said, they haven't really been clear about the reorganization being over, so it's always sort of hanging over me. I haven't had a stretch where it wasn't affecting me at least a little bit.
Compared with what is objectively happening with the reorganization, does your level of worry feel far greater than would normally be expected?

Yeah, I think it is. Um... most days, my mind just jumps around constantly. Like, I'll start out worrying about whether we'll hit the launch numbers, and then it shifts to whether someone on my team is about to quit. And then from there, I'm stressing about the mortgage, or... or a client renewal. It just feels like every small delay could turn into something major. So, yeah, it definitely feels like a lot more than what's actually going on.
Before the sales-division reorganization began, had you ever gone through a continuous six-month period of excessive, hard-to-control worry about several different areas of your life?

No, not that I can remember. Um... before the reorganization started, things were pretty normal. I mean, I had regular stress, but I never went through a long stretch like that where I was just constantly worrying about everything and couldn't control it. It wasn't like this back then.
